vulnerability.title: NoPrivateNetworkHttpClient checks only primary_ip, so hostnames that resolve into private subnets reach the transport and enable internal IP/port enumeration
vulnerability.category_l2: internal network address and port enumeration via unresolved hostnames in NoPrivateNetworkHttpClient

fix_commits.message: [HttpClient] Filter private IPs before connecting when Host == IP
fix_commits.role: first patch; adds a URL-host check but IpUtils::checkIp only matches literal IPs, so hostnames are still not resolved or blocked
second patch; resolves the URL host through the transport resolve closure or dns_get_record(A/AAAA) and checks the resolved address before connecting

location.verification_method: Static read of NoPrivateNetworkHttpClient.php at v5.4.45, v5.4.46 and v5.4.47, both fix commits, their regression tests, and peeled-tag ancestry checks; no PHP runtime, DNS resolver or network request was executed.

entry_point.description: Decorator entry point. Every wrapped request is expected to be filtered against PRIVATE_SUBNETS before the inner client may connect.

critical_operation.description: The subnet policy is enforced only inside the on_progress callback and only against $info['primary_ip'] (lines 82-89; the excerpt shows the opening check). The callback does not resolve the URL hostname, so a hostname that resolves into PRIVATE_SUBNETS is never compared against the blocked ranges; and when primary_ip is empty (for example before or during host resolution) the check is skipped entirely. The request is delegated to the inner client at line 94, so the transport still performs host resolution and connection attempts. The advisory describes the resulting behavior as internal IP/port enumeration. The first patch (v5.4.46) adds a URL-host check, but IpUtils::checkIp rejects non-IP hostnames, so DNS names remain unchecked; the second patch resolves the host and checks the resolved address before connecting.

trace.description: decorator receives the caller-supplied method, URL and options
caller on_progress is captured and wrapped, making the wrapper the only enforcement point
the check is gated on $info['primary_ip'] changing, not on the URL hostname
IpUtils::checkIp is applied to primary_ip only; no DNS resolution of the host is performed for this check
request proceeds to the wrapped client, which resolves and connects to the host

source_crosscheck.notes: The revised Symfony advisory and the GHSA page agree on the two-patch fix and on the real fixed releases 5.4.47, 6.4.15 and 7.1.8; the CNA record, NVD description and OSV ranges are stale and still end at 5.4.46, 6.4.14 and 7.1.7. Git history confirms the advisory: the first patch landed in 5.4.46/6.4.14/7.1.7 and the second in 5.4.47/6.4.15/7.1.8. Severity disagrees: NVD Primary is 4.3 MEDIUM with AC:L, while the CNA and GHSA use AC:H and 3.1 LOW. The canonical severity uses the NVD Primary metric; the canonical affected ranges and fixed releases use the revised advisory and GHSA, corroborated by git ancestry.

limitations: Single-reviewer dossier; not eligible for data/vulnerabilities.jsonl yet.

No PHP runtime, DNS query or HTTP request was executed. The claim that host resolution/connection behavior leaks internal IP and port information is taken from the advisory; the precise observable signal (timing, error, or connection result) was not measured.

The vulnerable snapshot is v5.4.45; the same snapshot is also the evaluation target for CVE-2024-50340 and CVE-2024-50345, which is legitimate because all three vulnerabilities exist at the same exact SHA.

The advisory's affected ranges were revised on 2024-11-13; versions 5.4.46, 6.4.14 and 7.1.7 are still affected. The CNA record, NVD description and OSV ranges still name those versions as fixed and are stale. The dossier uses the revised advisory and GHSA ranges, corroborated by git ancestry.
NVD has a Primary CVSS 3.1 metric of 4.3 MEDIUM; the CNA and GHSA carry 3.1 LOW with AC:H. The canonical score is the NVD Primary metric; the disagreement is recorded, not reconciled.
The GitHub advisory credits Linus Karlsson and Chris Smith; the Symfony blog credits only Linus Karlsson. This does not affect the technical fields.
The regression tests were read, not executed. testNoPrivateNetwork uses localhost and testNoPrivateNetworkWithResolve uses an explicit resolve map; neither exercises real DNS A/AAAA fallback.

The second patch changes the on_progress callback contract by adding an optional fourth argument. The dossier records the change but does not audit downstream callers for callbacks that declare a fixed arity.
The repository snapshot has 11040 tracked files and 150 ambiguous files; the language job is NEEDS_REVIEW, not a clean PASS.
No dynamic red/green test was run, so no reproduction_reference exists and the entry is grade B at best.

The advisory does not state whether every transport (curl, native, amp) reached on_progress with an empty primary_ip before connecting at v5.4.45; the fix adds hostname resolution to the decorator itself, which removes that dependence.

Independent language reproduction is approximate: the 3327 first-party PHP files can be matched under an explicit filter, but the byte total 11,755,821 differs from the snapshot's 11,758,368 by 2,547 bytes (0.02%), and 25.45% is the share of all nonbinary tracked bytes, not of all tracked bytes (PHP is 87.45% of the latter). The canonical language evidence stays the snapshot proposal; the reviewer's reproduction supports the PHP-primary conclusion.

The GitHub GHSA page's Weaknesses section shows 'No CWEs', while the CNA problemTypes, NVD weaknesses (Secondary) and OSV database_specific all list CWE-200. The canonical cwe_ids use the data-layer CWE-200.
open_questions: Which applications expose attacker-influenced URLs to NoPrivateNetworkHttpClient is application-specific; the component itself is a mitigation wrapper, and the advisory treats it as a security boundary.

The exact leak primitive (blind timing versus observable error/status differences) is not specified in the advisory and was not measured; the fixed code blocks before connection, which is consistent with enumeration through connection behavior.

required_before_promotion: An independent reviewer must read NoPrivateNetworkHttpClient::request at v5.4.45 and confirm that the only subnet check uses primary_ip and never resolves the URL hostname.

An independent reviewer must confirm that 296d4b34 and b4bf5afd are absent from v5.4.45, that the first patch alone still cannot block DNS names, and that both are ancestors of v5.4.47/v6.4.15/v7.1.8.
An independent reviewer must check the 4.3 MEDIUM NVD Primary metric against the 3.1 LOW CNA/GHSA metric, CWE-200, and the revised affected ranges.
No formal reviews.jsonl row may be written until a named independent reviewer returns a verdict.
